title: Adaptive Anchoring UX and Performance Signature Explorer
creator: Aisha Khandelwal
description: Add an 'Adaptive Anchoring' experience and a compact 'Performance Signature Explorer' in the Console model version selector. Purpose: help engineers and platform owners quickly choose and pin the most cost-effective, latency-safe model variant while surfacing risk signals (regressions, failure modes) and a confidence grade for automated recommendations. This is focused on improving onboarding workflows for new models and reducing manual trial-and-error when pinning versions for production routes.
background_and_rationale: Teams frequently struggle to pick a model version to pin because perf metrics are scattered across pages and lack a single risk/benefit summary. Current Console views show snapshots but don't recommend anchors or explain tradeoffs (cost vs p95 vs quality regression risk). This feature combines telemetry, small eval-set checks, and utilitarian UI to reduce churn on pins and decrease incidents caused by unexpected perf regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Explorer panel available from the version selector dropdown and model publish flow
Performance Signature shows p50, p95, median tokens-per-second, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated), error-rate, and eval-regression flag for each model version
Adaptive Anchoring suggests up to 3 candidate versions with an ordered confidence score and a short rationale sentence
Users can pin a version from the explorer without leaving the composer; pin action creates a publish entry in the timeline and an audit log event
Feature is gated by a feature flag and respects org-level RBAC (only curators/owners can perform pins if policy forbids it)
Telemetry events emitted for explorer_open, candidate_clicked, pin_attempted, pin_succeeded, and revert_pin
Automated smoke test validates explorer metrics render for a synthetic test model in staging
engineering_notes: Backend: requires new aggregated metrics endpoint combining runtime telemetry + eval regression signals (ENG-26540)
Front-end: new Explorer component in Version Selector with lazy loading and skeleton states
Runtime: ensure KV cache and batching heuristics are included in cost estimate calculation (see runtime-1.22 heuristics doc)
API contract: /v1/models/{model}/versions/{version}/signature returns metrics snapshot and confidence metadata
Telemetry: add explorer_open, candidate_selected, pin_requested, pin_confirmed, pin_reverted events to analytics pipeline
Privacy: do not include any raw prompt or user content in explorer payloads; only aggregated metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (FF off): Merge behind feature flag and smoke tests in staging
Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for internal orgs + 5 pilot customers (10% of console traffic) for 2 weeks
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% of orgs, monitor pin-change rate and revert frequency
Phase 3: Full rollout with opt-in educational tooltip and in-console tour
Rollback: FF toggles and automated revert if revert_rate > 8% or error_rate spikes
qa_checks: Explorer loads within 400ms for cached org queries and within 2s cold
Metrics match runtime dashboard within 5% tolerance for p95 and cost estimate
RBAC prevents unauthorized pins and shows informative tooltip
Audit log entry appears for every pin action with user id, timestamp, previous pin
Smoke test covers synthetic model in staging and asserts no Console errors
metrics_and_signals: Adoption: percentage of version selections initiated from Explorer (target 35% in first 6 weeks)
Pin stability: percent of pins that are reverted within 7 days (target < 10%)
Mean latency improvement for routes that used recommendations
Cost delta per 1M tokens across orgs that adopt suggestions
Incident reduction: number of production regressions attributed to pinned-version surprises
